Answer: We have known from the Puranas that even for a deity, it is about living happily in the concept of heaven for a certain period of time. That is also what is known from wise sages. That is our experience as well.
Question: Then, isn't it said in these Puranas and elsewhere that in the past, these deities were made to manifest, and great things were accomplished?

Answer: That is more or less true. When the knowledge, qualifications, and intellect of the writers are mixed into it, errors occur in the Puranas. Those who study such errors, accept them as truth, and practice them will face the same blunder. They are the ones who are said to commit worse mistakes than atheists. It will require a very difficult phase for their souls to attain liberation.
Question: What do you state as the reason for that?

Answer: Because this soul learns to act in this manner and remains somewhat aware and unaware of the results of its actions, it may fail to live a respectable life while alive. The reason for this is the arrogance of feeling that one has experienced and known many things. Beyond that, there is an unwillingness to acknowledge anyone else. With this, all their actions become wrong, and at the same time, they lead a life unsuitable for ordinary people. They will be unable to speak about highly spiritual people and will even reject them.

Many people of this kind can be seen in various places during the same period. Leaving their physical bodies, their souls will remain suspended in the atmosphere. They will not get a rebirth immediately. Standing there, they will gather souls lower than themselves to join them. Thus, they will form a group. They will trouble ordinary people and lead noble devotees astray.
Guruvani
October 1978
Question: Why was it stated in two different ways?

Answer: Ordinary people sometimes face afflictions from ghosts and evil spirits. If it is under the control of such a fallen yogi (*Yogabhrashta*), it becomes difficult to remove. If the person is a ritualist or a devotee, it will lead the ritualist astray in his rituals. For a devotee, it will first invoke the deity worshipped by the fallen yogi, or manifest a mixed form of the deity the devotee believes in, ultimately bringing the devotee to the position of the fallen yogi. Thus, after passing many ages, if any great souls are born, when these spirits go there to cause trouble, they might be liberated. Alternatively, with the birth of a Guru belonging to the lineage of Manu, such souls might attain liberation. If they still do not get it, that soul might wander in the atmosphere until the end of the eon (*Kalpa*).
Question: How do you determine this period of Manu?

Answer: The period of one Manu is seen in the Puranas and Vedas as seventy-one Chaturyugas. During these Chaturyugas, when Gurus belonging to the lineage of Manu are born here and there, they liberate such souls either because the spirits troubled them or because the Gurus themselves became aware of them. Only those belonging to the lineage of Manu have the authority to do this. Gurus who worship deities, or those who come to guide people to the righteous path for two thousand or three thousand years, do not have this authority.
Question: In which eras do such Gurus get born?
Answer: Such Gurus are born in all eras.
Question: How do humans understand this, and how do they deal with it in the world?

Answer: Gurus born in the *Satyayuga* only have the task of convincing the people, through writing and speaking, about the knowledge of how the world should function in specific ways. It is a time when people truly see and respect the deities. Nothing stands in conflict with each other. That is due to the uniqueness of the era. That is why it is named *Satyayuga*. As the period of *Tretayuga* begins, certain deviations start appearing among the people themselves.
Question: What is meant by saying "Mother, Father, Guru, God"?

Answer: The first Guru is the mother. We do not know the father. From pointing out and introducing the father, that process takes place through the mother to a certain extent. Then, to an extent, the father leads, up to the limit of his knowledge. Beyond that, the father points out the Guru. That Guru provides the experience of God. Thus, the Guru as mother, the Guru as father, the Guru who knows God, and God as Guru—in this way, from birth, one must climb the steps of knowledge, further knowledge, and ultimate knowledge to seek peace. That itself is the goal. That itself is liberation, and human birth is precisely for that.
Question: I wished to know your opinion about accepting *Sannyasa* (renunciation).

Answer: *Sannyasa* is not a ritual like tying the nuptial thread in a wedding. It has been written in some places in what we call our scriptures that it is so. Such things are distortions that crept into our true lives over time, like adding water to milk. *Sannyasa* is not retreating to some corner to escape from actions, like closing one's eyes to make it dark. The body is meant to perform actions. Even the worship of God is an action. Therefore, the duty of a *Sannyasi* is to handle the problems of society. It was like that in the past. In the holy land of Bharat, that was the duty of a *Sannyasi*. From the day hypocrisy started in the name of *Sannyasa*, the downfall of Bharat began.
Question: Previously, you had mentioned about the prayers to favorite deities (*Ishta Devata*) in certain places; it would be a blessing to hear about that.

Answer: I shall tell you. The father might be highly proficient in mantras, and a universal preceptor (*Lokacharya*) in tantra. The favorite deity (*Ishta Devata* or *Paradevata*) would be a fierce male or female entity claiming paternity or maternity over all ghosts and evil spirits. To destroy anyone in the land, they will perform sorcery inside the heads of cats or chickens. They will make a roasted chicken fly. The liquor of a whole tavern won't be enough; they will still call out, "Bring more, bring more." Upon hearing that call, all fourteen worlds will tremble. This is how the glories of one's ancestral position go. Even today, such boasting can be heard in some villages and towns.

Then the second stage. The father dies. There are minor troubles at home. What the astrologer who conducted the *Prashna* (astrological query) said, and what the maternal aunt's second son blurted out while in a trance, are exactly the same. There is not a single difference. The fiercely powerful father must be enshrined. The father will not let go. Thus, to purify the father, another sorcerer just like the father was brought in. Snapping fingers like purifying the *Koduveli* tuber, a chicken was sacrificed, and the father's spirit was invoked into a granite stone and consecrated under the shade of a tree in the compound. A lamp was lit, and prayers were offered. Needs were stated. Through dancing, swaying, and annual rituals, it became a custom. As generations passed, the dead sorcerer-father became a god.

Excluding today's Vedanta preachers who claim everything is Brahman, let me ask a question: where will this worship—which bears witness to the spiritual essence of this man who captured and worshipped all evil spirits, and who did nothing but create notorious rumors in the land—lead the future generations? Is this the worship of God? Is this Indian culture? Is this the spiritual guidance of this holy land?
Guruvani
November 1978
Question: What is the initial nature of devotion?

Answer: Attentiveness. There will be a nature of paying attention to whatever is seen. According to the Hindu tradition, there are numerous deities. In the beginning of devotion, the devotion towards gods and goddesses will keep changing. We might feel that we are good. In reality, if we observe closely, we will understand if there is anyone worse than us. A Guru is there to change the course of karma from previous births.
Question: When devotion arises, will there be any flaws in it?

Answer: When devotion arises, although great love and glory may come at first, there are some flaws in it too. That is—those living in the next house might have base qualities. Looking at them, one might say, "Alas, they are wretched people." They will also retort, "Oh! Such devotion—chanting starts as soon as it dawns." When all this devotion comes to us, some among lust, anger, greed, delusion, arrogance, pride, and jealousy will disappear, while some others will surge up.
Question: What is the reason for that?
Answer: Didn't I say that desire (*Kama*) stands at the forefront in devotion? It will eagerly jump forward for a good color, a good object, and everything else.
Question: You mentioned that three things can be understood through philosophical vision, didn't you? How can this be understood?

Answer: One can know it by paying special attention to its color. However, it is not the same for a devotee, a yogi, a wise man (jnani), and a man of action (karmi). If it is a devotee, they see everything through the Guru. If it is a yogi, they might wander off the path. If the Guru is there to guide closely, then let them wander. If it is a jnani, they can see with discrimination. However, for a karmi, it can be seen only when combined with their own effort.
Question: O Guru! What is the reason for attaining it in such various natures?

Answer: I shall explain. If it is a devotee, there is no sense of 'I'. They will surrender everything to the Guru. If it is a yogi, it will be in the manner of 'I am everything'. They will give priority to their own affairs. They will speak of everything trivially. No matter what thoughts arise, not denying anything and not blaming anything is one of the greatest fortunes.
Guruvani
December 1978

If we say we must become one, as long as this order of worship remains uninterrupted, it cannot be removed from the human community. At the same time, as long as the workers and institutions standing under the shade of these organizations do not stand with respect and devotion, its profound knowledge cannot be reclaimed. Even the society that carries the essence has not been able to do this. Denying and understanding anything from a distance will only be an understanding rooted in meaninglessness.
Question: What is the reason for you to say so?

Answer: After the Swami's samadhi, his fortieth-day bathing ceremony (Nalpathukuli Adiyanthiram) was not conducted. (There is such a ritual after the samadhi of a sanyasi). Why was it not conducted? That cannot be stated in this context. It will only help in creating agitation among the people. It was mentioned merely for the sake of knowing.

Another thing: In Sivagiri, known as the Swami's samadhi place, innocent sanyasis and innocent brahmacharis have had to experience situations for ten years in a manner that no one else could know how they happened. Although many among them are still alive today, a person who lives with the knowledge of having experienced it is the Retd. Ayurveda College Principal, Sri. V. Bhargavan Vaidyar.

All this originates from a culture that lacks the ability to respect and understand. Because of this, righteous sanyasis and brahmacharis vanished from the field of action. That continues even today. Apart from a few changes, it has not clearly resolved, and the disputes among the institutions caused by it have not ended even today. I merely mentioned these things as they are part of my daily experience. We, along with the people, still need to awaken and think so that this can deeply penetrate the very depths of the hearts of today's little children of the coming generations and be absorbed by them. I have a lot to say about all this.
Guruvani
